skill.name: completion-integrity
skill.description: Prevents shortcuts and cheating when completing tasks. Blocks commits with warning suppressions, commented tests, or deleted assertions.
skill.summary: Adds Git-hook checks that discourage skipped verification, deleted tests, and hidden warnings.
skill.author: ANcpLua

security_audit.summary: Two static findings are confirmed because SKILL.md documents bash commands that execute plugin-provided scripts for installation and manual checks. The other two findings are Markdown backtick false positives, and no prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Install instructions execute a shell script from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
remediation.suggestion: Document what install-git-hook.sh changes and require explicit user approval before running the command.

remediation.issue: Manual check instructions execute a plugin-provided shell script.
remediation.suggestion: State that integrity-check.sh is expected to be read-only and ask users to review it before execution.

static_findings.snippet: | Warning suppression (`#pragma warning disable`, `eslint-disable`) | Hides problems instead of fixi

finding_verdicts.reason: The install block instructs users or an agent to run a shell script with bash from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. In a community skill, that can modify local Git hooks and execute unreviewed script content.
The matched range is Markdown fencing and prose around a table, not executable shell or Ruby backtick evaluation. No command injection vector is present in that content.
The inline backticks describe warning-suppression examples in prose. They are not shell backticks and do not execute commands.
The manual check block instructs users or an agent to run integrity-check.sh with bash. The command is transparent and local, but it still executes plugin-provided code in the workspace.

content.value_statement: AI coding sessions can finish with skipped checks, deleted tests, or hidden warnings. This skill adds Git-hook integrity checks and clear verification rules.
actual_capabilities: Documents a Git pre-commit hook for integrity checks.
Flags warning suppressions that may hide unresolved problems.
Flags commented-out tests, deleted assertions, and deleted test files.
Identifies empty catch blocks and excess fresh TODO comments.
Provides a manual integrity check command for repository review.
Gives guidance for explaining legitimate false positives.
limitations: Requires the referenced CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT scripts to be present.
May flag legitimate warning suppressions that have valid context.
Covers the listed integrity patterns, not every code quality issue.
Does not replace running tests, linters, or security scans.

use_cases.title: Protect Code Review Quality
use_cases.description: Block commits that remove checks or hide warnings before review starts.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering teams using AI coding assistants

use_cases.title: Verify AI-Generated Fixes
use_cases.description: Check that an assistant fixed failures instead of commenting out tests or assertions.
use_cases.target_user: Developers working with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code

use_cases.title: Standardize Commit Discipline
use_cases.description: Give contributors a shared pre-commit rule set for completion integrity.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use completion-integrity while reviewing my latest Git changes. Identify warning suppressions, commented tests, deleted assertions, deleted test files, empty catch blocks, or fresh TODOs.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Integrity Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the completion-integrity manual check for this repository if it is available. Summarize any violations and propose fixes before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Before committing, inspect the diff with completion-integrity rules. Fix or explain each detected violation, then tell me what verification you ran.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Exception Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: A warning suppression may be necessary in this change. Evaluate whether the justification is strong enough for review, recommend safer alternatives, and list the remaining risk.

output_examples.input: The assistant tries to commit after commenting out a failing test.
output_examples.output: The commit is blocked. The response explains that commented tests must be fixed or removed with a reviewed reason.

output_examples.input: A change adds several new TODO comments and deletes assertions.
output_examples.output: The review highlights fresh TODOs and assertion removal as integrity violations, then asks for concrete fixes before completion.

output_examples.input: A suppression may be required for a platform-specific warning.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for a clear justification, confirms the warning cannot be fixed directly, and records the remaining review risk.

best_practices: Review community shell scripts before installing Git hooks.
Run normal tests and linters in addition to the integrity check.
Document necessary suppressions with clear reviewer-focused reasons.
anti_patterns: Commenting out failing tests to make a task appear complete.
Deleting assertions instead of fixing the behavior they protect.
Claiming work is complete without running meaningful verification.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks for warning suppressions, commented tests, deleted assertions, test file deletion, empty catch blocks, and excess fresh TODOs.

faq.question: Does it replace tests?
faq.answer: No. It supports integrity review, but you should still run tests, linters, and any required project checks.

faq.question: Can legitimate suppressions pass?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for a clear explanation that can convince a reviewer before accepting a suppression.

faq.question: Does it install automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents an install command, and users should review the referenced script before running it.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I do if it blocks a commit?
faq.answer: Fix the underlying issue, or document why the exception is necessary and suitable for reviewer approval.
